assumptions: The product remains a source-linked administrative completeness adapter and does not issue legal-entitlement decisions; a qualified specialist approves each project-specific ruleset.
A permissioned family-business project can provide pilot access, but that access is not treated as evidence of external demand, willingness to pay, or scalable acquisition.
PEF, KSeF, ERP, and document-management products remain systems of record, so the adapter must integrate with rather than replace them.
The stated pricing, delivery cost, configuration effort, renewal, and margin ranges are hypotheses rather than observed economics.
No reusable data right, exclusive authority relationship, adviser channel, or partner commitment is assumed until contractually established.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two or more unrelated paid pilots should identify the actual budget owner and measure baseline versus achieved rejection rate, administrator hours, days-to-payment, configuration and legal-review hours, support burden, gross margin, sales cycle, CAC payback, and renewal or referral into the next project; one should also demonstrate authorized integration and reusable-pattern rights.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Polish public-works payment rules create a recurring evidence gate, and official guidance identifies concrete cross-document defects that delay requests. Reframing the product as a source-linked exception adapter instead of another document portal is a coherent insight, although adjacent construction systems already recognize much of the workflow problem.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Delayed or blocked payment is acute for cash-constrained contractors, and GDDKiA documents recurring evidence defects and material payment-protection activity. The evidence does not isolate how often curable documentation gaps cause losses, identify the budget owner, or establish willingness to pay 1,500-4,000 PLN per project each month; free and lower-priced substitutes make the premium uncertain rather than disproven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Setup fees plus recurring active-project fees can monetize repeated payment draws, and software-assisted exception handling could eventually support healthy margins. However, project-specific legal configuration, stakeholder onboarding, integration, support, project closure churn, and slow trust-based sales may keep gross margin and CAC payback service-like; the 150-project founder-wealth path is arithmetically plausible but operationally unproven.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish public construction sits inside a large procurement market, while renewable and electrical packages with multiple subcontractors form a sufficiently narrow first use case. Family-business access can make one pilot reachable, but the number of externally addressable projects, reachable software spend, and whether the initial participant is the actual payer remain unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Authority-specific mappings and source-linked exception views offer a sharper position than generic storage or invoice submission. Yet PEF is free and PlanRadar, Archdesk, and PROGPOL already occupy adjacent records, approvals, subcontractor, and payment workflows; without an exclusive channel or uniquely reliable corpus, a narrow leader could be copied, bundled, or bypassed.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven ruleset and integration pattern could extend from renewable and electrical packages to other public-works trades, authorities, contract forms, and eventually related compliance or payment workflows. Each adjacency may require new legal review and configuration, so expansion is credible but may not inherit the economics as easily as the common evidence-graph architecture suggests.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Counsel-approved templates, integrations, audit history, and labeled rejection-and-cure patterns could accumulate into switching costs and a useful data advantage. Reuse permission is unknown, projects terminate, authority rules vary, and incumbent systems can reproduce a completeness layer, leaving the proposed moat contingent rather than established.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A reliable pre-submission exception view could save administrator time and, more importantly, avoid costly payment holds while preserving source-level auditability. No measured reduction in rejected draws, labor, or days-to-cash shows that this improvement is large enough to change buying behavior, and legal review still limits automation of the hardest cases.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Persistent statutory evidence requirements, digitized public-procurement records, APIs, and capable extraction tools make a narrow adapter more feasible now. The same digitization supports free government infrastructure and mature construction-software vendors, and the supplied evidence shows no new deadline or regulatory discontinuity that forces near-term purchase.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Permissioned family-business access provides a realistic route to discovery and one pilot without relying on a personal brand. Repeatable acquisition through advisers or contract administrators is unvalidated, while external sales require sensitive-data trust, multi-party onboarding, and a clear economic buyer; these conditions can produce long cycles and unattractive CAC for project-bounded revenue.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data-science skills, AI leverage, family access, and 60,000 PLN pilot budget fit a narrow evidence-graph prototype. Execution remains near the part-time ceiling and depends on qualified legal review, participant authorization, granular permissions, secure handling of sensitive records, integrations, and disciplined wording that prevents users from mistaking completeness for legal entitlement.

highest_value_structural_change: Concentrate on one high-volume authority and contract-form family, package a counsel-approved exception ruleset as an embedded module for an incumbent ERP/DMS or contract-administrator channel, and price at the contractor portfolio level; this would reduce per-project customization and reacquisition while making distribution and accumulating evidence patterns more defensible.
main_structural_strength: A recurring statutory payment-evidence gate creates a concrete control point where a source-linked exception graph can prevent high-cost administrative failures without displacing existing systems of record.
primary_score_limiter: The opportunity has not yet shown that heterogeneous, legally reviewed project configurations can be delivered and sold repeatedly at premium project pricing with attractive margin, CAC payback, and project-to-project retention.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Free PEF infrastructure and established products such as PlanRadar, Archdesk, and PROGPOL already cover substantial adjacent submission, document, approval, subcontractor, and payment workflows, while published PlanRadar pricing challenges the proposed specialized project fee.
